similar_questions.stem: The dimensional formula for efficiency is;

options.E: None

explanation_steps:
Efficiency ($$ \eta $$) is defined as the ratio of Output Work to Input Work (or Power out to Power in). 

**Formula:** 
$$ \eta = \frac{W_{out}}{W_{in}} $$

Since it is a ratio of two identical physical quantities (Work/Work), it is dimensionless. Its dimensional formula is $$ M^0 L^0 T^0 $$. None of the given options match.

questions.stem: An airplane takes off at an angle of 45° to the horizontal. If the horizontal component of its velocity is 200 m/s, then the vertical component of its velocity and resultant speed in m/s are, respectively. (Take cos 45° = sin 45° = 0.707.)
explanation_steps: At 45°, vx = v cos 45° and vy = v sin 45°, so vy = vx = 200 m/s.
Resultant speed v = 200 / 0.707 = 282.9 m/s, matching 282.8. Answer: C.

similar_questions.stem: If a projectile is launched at an angle of $$ 30^\circ $$ with the horizontal, what is the vertical component of the initial velocity, in m/s, if the initial speed is 20 m/s?
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify Given Values.**
*   Initial speed ($$ v $$) = 20 m/s
*   Angle ($$ \theta $$) = $$ 30^\circ $$

**Step 2: Use Vector Resolution Formula.**
The vertical component ($$ v_y $$) is calculated as: $$ v_y = v \cdot \sin(\theta) $$

**Step 3: Calculate.**
$$ v_y = 20 \times \sin(30^\circ) $$
We know $$ \sin(30^\circ) = 0.5 $$
$$ v_y = 20 \times 0.5 = 10 \text{ m/s} $$

questions.stem: Which of the following statements is not correct?

options.A: In projectile motion, at the peak of the trajectory, both the vertical and horizontal components of velocity are zero.
options.B: If an object is moving in uniform circular motion, it is accelerating.
options.C: As the radius of the circular path increases, the centripetal acceleration decreases, provided that the velocity remains the same.
options.D: In the motion of the moon around the earth, the force that provides the necessary centripetal acceleration is the gravitational attraction of the earth.
options.E: In a projectile motion, the horizontal component of velocity is always constant if air resistance is neglected.

explanation_steps: At the peak, only the vertical component is zero. The horizontal component stays constant if air resistance is neglected.
B–E are correct. Answer: A.
tips: Exceptions (Hg liquid, Na/K low melting) do not change the general rule.

similar_questions.stem: When the resultant force acting on a body is zero, the body is in translational equilibrium. Related to Newton's first law this is a statement of

options.A: principle of moments.
options.B: first condition of equilibrium.
options.C: second condition of equilibrium.
options.D: rotational equilibrium.
options.E: circular equilibrium.

explanation_steps: The textbook (G10 p.36): when the resultant force on a body is zero it is in translational equilibrium – the first condition of equilibrium; when the resultant moment is zero it is in rotational equilibrium – the second condition (principle of moments, G10 p.30).
A, C and D all describe the moment (rotational) condition. Answer: B.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following statements concerning friction is wrong?

options.A: Friction is reduced when surfaces are highly polished by oil, grease or graphite.
options.B: Friction is reduced when one body rolls over the surface of another body.
options.C: Static friction between two surfaces of bodies is larger than sliding friction.
options.D: Coefficient of friction is the ratio of frictional force to the normal reaction force.
options.E: The larger the value of the coefficient of friction, the smaller is the friction present.

explanation_steps: Lubricants (oil, grease, graphite) and rolling (ball bearings, wheels) reduce friction (G9 p.175–177) – A and B are correct.
Maximum static friction is larger than sliding (kinetic) friction (G9 p.177–179) – C is correct.
μ = f/N (G9 p.180–183) – D is correct; so f = μN: a LARGER μ means MORE friction. E is wrong. Answer: E.

similar_questions.stem: A 200N force is needed to expand a spring 20mm from its equilibrium position. Then the spring’s constant equals to:

options.E: None

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Identify values.**
- $$ F = 200N $$
- $$ x = 20mm = 0.02m $$

**Step 2: Use Hooke's Law.**
$$ F = kx \Rightarrow k = \frac{F}{x} $$

similar_questions.stem: Two lenses, of power 1 Diopter and 3 Diopter, are placed in contact, the focal length of the combination in meter is:
explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Find the total power ($$ P_{total} $$).**
When lenses are in contact, their powers add up: $$ P_{total} = P_1 + P_2 = 1 + 3 = 4 D $$.

similar_questions.stem: Red light whose wavelength is 300nm. Its momentum in kg m/s and frequency in hertz respectively are;

options.E: None

explanation_steps:
**Step 1: Calculate Frequency ($$ f $$).**
$$ f = c / \lambda $$
$$ f = (3 \times 10^8) / (300 \times 10^{-9}) = 1 \times 10^{15} \text{ Hz} $$

**Step 2: Calculate Momentum ($$ p $$).**
Using de Broglie relation: $$ p = h / \lambda $$
$$ p = (6.63 \times 10^{-34}) / (300 \times 10^{-9}) $$
$$ p = 0.0221 \times 10^{-25} = 2.21 \times 10^{-27} \text{ kg} \cdot \text{m/s} $$.

similar_questions.stem: Which of the following statements concerning friction is wrong?

options.A: Friction is reduced when surfaces are highly polished by oil, grease or graphite.
options.B: Friction is reduced when one body rolls over the surface of another body.
options.C: Static friction between two surfaces of bodies is larger than sliding friction.
options.D: Coefficient of friction is the ratio of frictional force to the normal reaction force.
options.E: The larger the value of the coefficient of friction, the smaller is the friction present.

explanation_steps: Lubricants (oil, grease, graphite) and rolling (ball bearings, wheels) reduce friction (G9 p.175–177) – A and B are correct.
Maximum static friction is larger than sliding (kinetic) friction (G9 p.177–179) – C is correct.
μ = f/N (G9 p.180–183) – D is correct; so f = μN: a LARGER μ means MORE friction. E is wrong. Answer: E.

questions.stem: Choose the incorrect statement from the following.

options.B: The charges on two capacitors connected in series depend on the value of the capacitors.
options.C: The equivalent capacitance of two capacitors connected in parallel is the sum of the individual capacitances.
options.D: The potential difference on two capacitors connected in parallel is the same.
options.E: The relation between the charge Q, the potential difference across the capacitor V, and the capacitance C is Q = CV.

explanation_steps: Capacitors in series carry the same charge. The charge does not depend on which capacitor it is.
A, C, D and E are correct. Answer: B.

explanation_steps:
The formula for hydrostatic pressure is $$ P = \rho g h $$.

similar_questions.stem: A man of mass 40kg climbs a wall 2m high, the work done due to gravity is;

options.E: None

explanation_steps:
**Given:**
$$ m = 40kg $$, $$ h = 2m $$, $$ g = 10m/s^2 $$

**Formula:**
Work done against gravity is equal to the change in Potential Energy.
$$ W = mgh $$

**Calculation:**
$$ W = 40 \times 10 \times 2 = 800J $$

questions.stem: When a nucleus emits an alpha-particle, which of the following does not change?

options.A: The mass number.
options.B: The atomic number.
options.C: The number of neutrons.
options.D: The chemical identity of the nucleus.
options.E: The total charge of the nucleus plus the emitted alpha-particle.

explanation_steps: An alpha particle is a helium nucleus, so mass number falls by 4, atomic number by 2, and neutron number by 2. The element changes.
Charge is conserved for the nucleus plus the alpha particle. Answer: E.

options.C: the atomic number of the daughter nucleus decreases by 1.
options.D: the daughter nucleus occupies a different position in the periodic table.

explanation_steps: β⁻ emission raises the atomic number by 1; it does not decrease it.
Mass number is unchanged, charge is conserved, and the daughter is a different element. The incorrect statement is C.

similar_questions.stem:
A laser source emits light of frequency 8 × 10¹⁴ Hz at a rate of 300 J/min. The average number of photons per second emitted by the source is
[h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s]
similar_questions.stem_tex: A laser source emits light of frequency $8\times10^{14}$ Hz at a rate of 300 J/min. The average number of photons per second emitted by the source is $\left[h = 6.63\times10^{-34}\ \mathrm{J\,s}\right]$
explanation_steps: Power: 300 J/min ÷ 60 s = 5.0 J/s (5.0 W).
Energy of one photon: E = hf = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ × 8 × 10¹⁴ = 5.30 × 10⁻¹⁹ J (G12 p.101–103).
Photons per second = 5.0 / 5.30 × 10⁻¹⁹ = 9.43 × 10¹⁸. Answer: D.
